title: RTX 4090 native lane: the host-KV pool that keeps two long sessions and their state
method: One binary, one host, one workload: two sessions of about 125,900 input tokens alternating turns, then explicit checkpoints, a graceful stop through the lane's own --stop-event path, a restart, and a resume of each session's planted desk code. Only the host-KV pool size changed between arms; every other argument matches the shipped configuration.

device_kv.note: a session at the 131,072-token ceiling needs about 5.02 GiB of KV, so the shipped 4 GiB host pool cannot hold even one

arms.automatic_export: refused while both sessions were live (program refused continuation export)
arms.graceful_stop: saved 1, refused 1 - 'the shutdown could not save 1 live session(s); their state is lost'
arms.source: EXP-041, 2026-09-16, the lane's own managed stop receipt

arms.reuse_lost: 2 of 8: the second session's continuation re-prefilled from root in 91 s every round
arms.note: holds one ceiling session, so whichever session is not device-resident loses its KV

arms.graceful_stop: shutdown: saved 2, nothing to save 0, refused 0

arms.result: cudaMallocHost failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
arms.note: the pinned-memory ceiling on this 32.4 GiB host, not a shortage of free RAM (27.6 GiB was free). 11 GiB is the largest pool that pins here.

finding: The shipped RTX 4090 host-KV pool is 4096 MiB - half the engine's own 8192 MiB default and below the 5.02 GiB a single ceiling-sized session needs. That one number causes all three symptoms: an evicted session's KV is dropped rather than spilled, so its next turn re-prefills from root; an export needs live KV, so the automatic checkpoint is refused; and a graceful stop can then only save the session that happens to be resident, reporting the other as lost. At 11264 MiB - enough for both sessions at once - reuse holds, both sessions checkpoint, the graceful stop saves both, and both resume exactly after a restart.
restore_needs_the_whole_sum: Restore is stricter than live alternation. A live pair only needs the pool to hold the session that is not device-resident; restore materialises every checkpointed session into host extents, so it needs the pool to hold their sum. That is why two sessions both restored here at 11264 MiB (2 x 5.02 GiB) while the RTX 5090's 16 GiB pool, which holds one 8.6 GiB bf16 session with room to spare, admits only one of two at restart (omp-ninfer#40).
